nodes.title: The main loop reviewed the 26 web screens by eye at cee4313: layout, mobile behaviour and honesty are strong, but developer text leaks into the UI on 4 of the 7 screens it opened in full.
nodes.method: Read the desktop contact sheet of all 26 screens plus 7 full-size shots (agent-stack-d, today-m, campaign-draft-d, call-m, operator-plan-d, contacts-import-m and the desktop sheet) from product/web/shots after cee4313; web.test.ts 8/8 and ui-contract --strict 82/82 run locally.
nodes.value: Leaks: approval-card args (inrMilli 500000), 'by wallet.topup', tool developer summaries, campaign blocker text with tool ids and rule codes, 'Ran v2-flashlite', 'Settlement None', 'Analysis: failed' with no reason, '1 guarded opt-outs', a duplicate 'Not measured' chip, and 'Click' on mobile

nodes.title: No tool id, raw argument name, internal code or milli-unit ever reaches a person in the UI. Server messages meant for people are plain sentences; codes stay machine-readable alongside them.
nodes.rationale: The product promise is world-class and usable by any business owner. Text like 'To fix: number.search then number.rent' or 'inrMilli 500000' reads as broken software and hides what the person must do. The structural fix is server blockers and refusals carrying {code, message, why, fix:{tool,label}}, plus a rendered-text test that fails on tool-id patterns.
nodes.reverse_if: never for end-user screens; a developer or API-console view may show codes behind an explicit 'details' toggle
